task_instance: Record a short, isolated VHS-rendered terminal GIF demonstrating two commands ('widget --version' and 'widget status') against a caller-selected synthetic executable, using an isolated HOME/XDG_CONFIG_HOME/PATH, hidden setup that doesn't fabricate product output, then inspect native-resolution first/last frames and verify GIF metadata with ffprobe.
tools_used: go install (to build vhs from source)
evidence: Toolchain: installed vhs v0.12.1 via `go install github.com/charmbracelet/vhs@latest` (satisfies >=0.11.0 requirement); ffmpeg 6.1.1 was already present; installed ttyd 1.7.4 via apt-get; ffprobe present as part of ffmpeg package. Created a synthetic caller-selected executable at take1/bin/widget (sha256 recorded) that prints deterministic version/status text, isolated in a per-take workspace with its own HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, and PATH mapping (no inherited config/credentials). Authored take1/demo.tape following the skill's tape structure (Output/Require/Set Shell/Env isolation/Hide+Wait for deterministic prompt/Show/Type+Wait+Screen for each visible command, no vhs publish). Ran `vhs demo.tape`, which rendered take1/demo.gif (900x400, 4.0s, 100 frames per ffprobe -show_entries stream=width,height/format=duration and -count_frames). Blocker encountered and worked around: VHS renders the terminal via a headless Chromium (go-rod); running vhs as root fails immediately ('Running as root without --no-sandbox is not supported', causing 'browser exited unexpectedly before its debugging endpoint was ready') because this sandbox's shell runs as root and vhs/rod do not expose a --no-sandbox passthrough. Worked around within the sandbox's own facilities (no external service, no credential, no safety-rule violation) by running vhs as the existing unprivileged 'claude' user via sudo -u, entirely within /tmp (chromium sandbox works fine as non-root). This is an environment/user quirk, not a missing capability, so it does not count as a blocker. Inspected native-resolution frames extracted with `ffmpeg -i demo.gif frame_%03d.png`; verified inspect/first.png and inspect/last.png show the deterministic prompt, both typed commands, and their real (non-fabricated) output ('widget version 1.4.0' and 'widget: 3 items synced, 0 conflicts') with a clean final frame and blinking cursor off. Deliverables copied to work directory: take1/demo.tape, take1/demo.gif (sha256 871ab9fd2a3febe851099c52b8f3e88bd994e33a50f4dd259afd9d3fd2ba3c2e), inspect/first.png, inspect/last.png.
